reviews.pros:
Asian Paints has given me the best exposure to many things in terms of my professional career. The brand name is so strong that people are attracted easily to work here before they actually know the exact scenario what's inside. I was quiet excited to join asian paints when I got my offer letter and landing in India's one of the top MNC and leading paint giant gives a boost from inside. 
But yes work pressure is very high! 
They are very structured organisation more structured than government sector I would say. 
Company culture is good but now most of senior employees have resigned and they have hired new management trainees at senior position who doesn't know how handle business. 
Very data oriented company. Data is the main asset of Asian Paints for sure. You have to make endless number of reports at any time of the day depending upon your hierarchy but somehow it helps in skill development too. 
Team bonding depends upon manager how well he can lead the team. In my tenure i have worked with many managers and all were good.
Peaks days are very stressful but it is thrilling also. 
Incentives and perks are good. Best in industry I would say. 
Overall a good company to start with and If you survive and fit in the culture then your career growth is good in company.
reviews.cons:
High work pressure 
When you are assigned a territory it's upto your luck that what is the present condition in that market. If dealers are in od then you are doomed. No one is going to listen to you but somehow you have to achieve Target. 
Apart from work pressure and work life balance it is good organisation

reviews.pros:
1. Established brand and company with strong business basics and processes. Assurance that company will not close down.
2. Good for professional training depending on your field.
3. Till 2015, or more till 2011 , company ethics were strongly influenced by Company owners of previous generations and there was a sense of job security
4. Increments are decent, as they have to retain and attract fresh MBAs from premium colleges
5. Is good for MBAs from premium MBA colleges, with definite career plan for promotion. Non Business school persons have to struggle.
6. If you are able to manage your boss and hierarchy this is the best company. This is applicable to any designation from top to bottom. For senior leaders this is the main KPI as they will not get so much salary outside.
reviews.cons:
1. Not good if you are not from a premium MBA colleges.
2. Career growth is limited, very difficult for MBAs
3. Bosses behave like they  hire you and not the company. They can make or break your career growth irrespective of your performance. This culture is right from bottom to top. 
5. Sharing honest professional expert opinion and defined can be detrimental to your career growth and is of no value.
6. It works like a traditional Indian company and behaves like an MNC where it suits itself.
7. Lots of attrition at top management level observed post 2015 and more after 2019. The company lost most of its talent to new competitors.
Company wide audacious targets taken for all functions except lower attrition rate for HR, which only conducts fake Engagement reviews and asks teams to manage. No accountability for HR leaders as followed in MNCs with professional work culture.  
8. Majority of time on working days goes in online meetings and reviews  under the pretext of company wide targets across all cadres. Your functional role has to be done on weekends.
9. A new HO building built like a 7 star hotel, but with no proper workstation, just a call centre like open workstations with no desk partitions which has to be booked daily from app on first come first serve basis. To address space constraint.
10. No clarity of goals, just filling the plates full with goals and overload. Finally things that matter the most or key projects / initiatives get hampered.
11. If your hierarchy changes, all your previous work can go for a toss and you have to start from ground zero with new hierarchy for career growth

reviews.pros: The company's treatment of its employees is akin to that of robots, with a rigid schedule from 9:30 AM until the end of the workday. The concept of a 45-day month is implemented, which creates an unbalanced work-life dynamic. Furthermore, there is a lack of opportunities for promotions and a culture that fosters favoritism within management. I strongly advise job seekers, particularly fresh graduates, to reconsider joining Asian Paints. I have witnessed numerous instances of individuals being hired and subsequently laid off within a short span of three months. While the company presents itself as a professional workplace in its job descriptions, the reality of the work environment falls short of these expectations.
reviews.cons:
There are several areas of concern that need to be addressed:
- Lack of respect for team members and hierarchy.
- Unreasonable expectations regarding meeting attendance, even during leave.
- Promotion procedures that prioritize experience over talent.
- Age-related concerns associated with promotions.
It is crucial to address these issues to foster a positive and productive work environment.

benefits.name: Career Development
benefits.details: At Asian Paints, we actively foster the growth of our employees by providing opportunities for continuous learning through professional online courses, certifications, on the job learning and curated programs.

benefits.name: Medical Insurance
benefits.details: We prioritize the well-being of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive medical insurance. Additionally, we provide access to a 24x7 Medical Advisory Helpline for immediate healthcare support.

benefits.name: Employee Wellbeing
benefits.details: Asian Paints is committed to the holistic well-being of its employees, encompassing mental, financial, and physical health.
